newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Unknown Arab group says it killed land dealer.
newsitem.headline: Unknown Arab group says it killed land dealer.

text.p: A previously unknown Palestinian group has claimed responsibility for killing an Arab who sold land to Jews, a newspaper editor said on Sunday.

An anonymous caller, speaking in Arabic, told the Palestinian daily al-Hayat al-Jadidah newspaper that the Keepers of the Holy Land Group shot Ali Mohammed Jumhour near Ramallah in the West Bank on Saturday because of his dealings.

Jumhour, 34, was the third land dealer found dead in the West Bank since Palestinian Justice Minister Freih Abu Medeen said last month Palestinians who sold land to Jews were traitors and would face the death penalty.

"The caller said his group, Keepers of the Holy Land, shot Jumhour dead because he sold land to Jews," Hafez al-Barghouthi, the newspaper's editor-in-chief, told Reuters. He said the caller had also contacted PLO police and other local newspapers.
All three victims were shot in the head at close range. Jumhour and another land dealer, 60 year-old Harbi Abu Sarah, were killed in Rafat near Ramallah, a village still under Israeli occupation.
The third, Farid Bashiti, was killed in al-Tireh village, also in the Ramallah area.
Israeli officials have said they suspect Palestinian President Yasser Arafat's administration is involved in the killings but PLO officials deny it.

"This is nonsense, the Authority is not involved in the killing of those dealers, brokers, traitors," Abu Medeen told reporters in self-ruled Gaza. "I accuse the Israelis, and I'm sure there is a finger of an Israeli in this assassination."

Abu Medeen said the Palestinian Authority had activated a Jordanian military law that once prohibited the sale of land to Jews. The new ban followed a crisis in PLO-Israeli peace moves over construction of a Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem in March.

"It's a law. Those suspected of selling land will be questioned, interrogated, and then according to the law, the judge will decide maybe to confiscate their property, maybe to sentence them to life imprisonment or maybe the penalty will reach the death penalty," Abu Medeen said.
Israel's Public Security Minister Avigdor Kahalani said he ordered police to give top priority to investigating Jumhour's killing.

Last week, Abu Medeen said the PLO was interrogating seven to 12 Palestinians suspected of selling land to Israelis. The PLO said the ban is needed to curb Jewish settlement in the Gaza Strip and the West bank, including East Jerusalem, that could strengthen Israeli claims to sovereignty.
Washington and an international human rights group have urged Arafat to forbid retribution against land dealers.
